newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thousands of Karen refugees flee into Thailand.
newsitem.headline: Thousands of Karen refugees flee into Thailand.

text.p: More than 16,000 Karen refugees have streamed into Thailand a day after Burmese troops attacked key Karen National Union guerrilla camps in Burma, Thai officials said on Thursday.

Border Patrol Police sources based in Umphang district of Thailand's northern Take province told Reuters the refugees had scattered in the jungle. On Wednesday, about 2,000 refugees were reported by the Thai army to have crossed over.
"They keep coming and I think the number will swell up to more than the 16,000 soon," a police source said.
Burmese troops on Wednesday attacked three KNU mobile camps in Burma's eastern jungle with mortars and artillery and dispersed about 4,000 KNU guerrillas, Thai military sources said.
About 70,000 ethnic Karen refugees, who fled fighting inside Burma, have been living in sprawling refugee camps along Thailand's border with Burma for years.
The refugees are family members and followers of the KNU which has been fighting the Burmese military government for greater autonomy for the Karen state since Burmese independence in 1948.

KNU, a predominantly Christian group, used to be the strongest among a dozen ethnic minority rebel groups fighting Rangoon. It has refused to lay down arms and rejected peace overtures from the Burmese government.
But in 1995, the KNU suffered a major setback when Buddhist members of the group mutinied, split from the mainstream and formed the Democratic Karen Buddhist Army (DKBA).
The DKBA, said to be backed by Rangoon, recently launched attacks against KNU camps and Karen refugees close to the Thai border.
